GOT QUESTIONS?

🇳🇿 Study in New Zealand FAQs

Answers to common questions about degree options, 3 year post study work visas, proof of funds, and living in New Zealand.

Interactive New Zealand Student FAQ Desk
Select any question to expand
Q1 Why study in New Zealand?
All 8 public universities in New Zealand are ranked in the top 3% worldwide in QS World University Rankings, offering safe environments, high standard of living, and clear post study work pathways.
Q2 How long is the Post Study Work Visa (PSWV) in New Zealand?
Graduates with a degree (bachelor's, master's, or PhD) qualify for a 3 year open Post Study Work Visa allowing them to work for any employer anywhere in New Zealand.
Q3 Can international students work while studying in New Zealand?
Yes. Full time tertiary students can work up to 20 hours per week during term time and full time during scheduled university vacations.
Q4 What are the IELTS / PTE requirements for NZ student visas?
Bachelor's degrees generally require IELTS 6.0 (no band less than 5.5) or PTE equivalent. Master's degrees require IELTS 6.5 (no band less than 6.0).
Q5 How much financial proof is required for a New Zealand student visa?
You need to demonstrate NZD 20,000 per year for living expenses in addition to your tuition fee payments, through bank deposits or FTS (Funds Transfer Scheme).
Q6 What is the Funds Transfer Scheme (FTS)?
FTS is an option established by Immigration New Zealand and ANZ bank to help students transfer living funds securely and show genuine financial capability.
Q7 How much does tuition cost in New Zealand?
Undergraduate tuition ranges from NZD 26,000 to NZD 38,000 per year. Postgraduate tuition ranges from NZD 30,000 to NZD 48,000 per year depending on the discipline.
Q8 Does studying in New Zealand lead to Permanent Residency (PR)?
Graduates can gain skilled employment experience during their PSWV and qualify for PR under the Skilled Migrant Category (SMC) or Green List Straight to Residence pathways.
